summary:
Static/config + unit-test verification for the Expo max-SDK override permission-conflict fix on branch feat/v098 (PR #37). No device, no backend API — all five review items pass. (1) Prebuild in isolated /tmp/pb2 (symlinked node_modules from /app/frontend/node_modules, source tar'd from /app/frontend) completed cleanly ('Finished prebuild'). The generated /tmp/pb2/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml declares exactly:
  line 7:  <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" tools:node="remove"/>
  line 14: <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" tools:node="remove"/>
 Both have tools:node="remove" and NEITHER carries an android:maxSdkVersion attribute, so the ExpoMaxSdkOverride plugin can no longer find two conflicting declarations to warn about. (2) frontend/src/components/PhotoPick.tsx:14 pickSmallPhoto() and frontend/src/core/paperFiles.ts:76 pickPaperPhoto() both use the exact pattern `Platform.OS === "android" ? { granted: true } : await ImagePicker.requestMediaLibraryPermissionsAsync()`; paperFiles.ts imports Platform from react-native at line 1. Repo-wide grep for READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE / WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE across app/, src/, and plugins/ returns ONLY the two assertions in src/core/storagePerms.test.ts — no runtime code requests either permission anywhere. (3) Regression suites: `yarn test` → 252 pass / 0 fail (duration 2.82 s), `npx tsc --noEmit` → exit 0 (clean), `node --test .github/scripts/*.test.js frontend/plugins/*.test.js` → 30 pass / 0 fail. (4) Other-work regression (code-review + unit tests only, no runtime): src/core/syncStamp.ts (stampChanges, mergeRows, tombstones), src/core/merge.ts (mergeDB re-exported through backup.ts), src/core/store.tsx:200 wires update() → stampChanges with a readOnly guard, src/core/selfCheck.ts + app/selfcheck.tsx (ConfirmSheet confirms the bank-switch-on fix at selfcheck.tsx:126-135), and the Settings row at app/(tabs)/settings.tsx:564 uses testID="settings-self-check" and router.push("/selfcheck"). Both syncStamp.test.ts and selfCheck.test.ts are part of the 252 passing tests. (5) `git diff origin/main..HEAD` is EMPTY for all guarded files (frontend/src/core/lockPolicy.ts, lockSettings.ts, security.ts, frontend/src/components/LockGate.tsx, DocumentContent.tsx, frontend/src/core/paperViewerPath.ts, paperViewerUri.ts, documentViewerCopy.ts) — 0 lines of diff — and CHANGELOG.md diff vs origin/main is also 0 lines. The actual 'ExpoMaxSdkOverride WARNING' line only surfaces during a Gradle build; that confirmation can only come from the GitHub Actions APK job and is outside this container's reach — reported as a limitation per the agent-to-agent context note.
critical_code_review_comments: app.json blockedPermissions now covers the two storage permissions the Expo max-SDK override plugin was complaining about; because blockedPermissions emits <uses-permission ... tools:node="remove"/> (verified in /tmp/pb2 manifest lines 7 and 14), both the stale maxSdkVersion-tagged and un-tagged declarations are stripped during manifest merging, which is exactly what resolves the plugin's 'Found 2 permission(s) with conflicting android:maxSdkVersion declarations' warning.

PhotoPick.pickSmallPhoto and paperFiles.pickPaperPhoto both short-circuit the media-library permission request on Android with `Platform.OS === "android" ? { granted: true } : await ImagePicker.requestMediaLibraryPermissionsAsync()`. This is the right call for Android 13+ because the system photo picker returns an opaque URI without needing READ_MEDIA_IMAGES / READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, so asking for it only re-introduces the permission entry we just blocked. iOS still requests the permission.

paperFiles.ts correctly imports Platform from react-native at the top of the file (line 1), so the Android branch compiles under the current ts config — reflected in `npx tsc --noEmit` returning clean.

src/core/storagePerms.test.ts is a tight guard-rail: it reads app.json directly and asserts both strings are present in blockedPermissions, and asserts the exact `Platform.OS === "android" ? { granted: true } : await ImagePicker.requestMediaLibraryPermissionsAsync()` regex is present in both pick files. If either backslide ever happens the test suite breaks loudly.

No runtime code in app/, src/, or plugins/ references READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE or WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE strings — the only hits are the two assertions inside storagePerms.test.ts, confirming the two permissions are only declared via the blockedPermissions path in app.json.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Prebuild verification pattern that worked here: `rm -rf /tmp/pb2 && mkdir /tmp/pb2 && cd /app/frontend && tar --exclude=node_modules --exclude=android --exclude=ios -cf - . | (cd /tmp/pb2 && tar xf -) && ln -s /app/frontend/node_modules /tmp/pb2/node_modules && cd /tmp/pb2 && CI=1 npx expo prebuild --platform android --no-install`. Never run `expo prebuild` inside /app/frontend itself — it mutates package.json and writes an android/ dir. The generated manifest to grep lives at /tmp/pb2/android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml. The Gradle-time 'ExpoMaxSdkOverride WARNING' is only observable in GitHub Actions, so document that as a limitation rather than trying to run Gradle in this container.
rca_of_issue: Root cause (as fixed by E1): autolinked Expo modules (expo-image-picker on older platform targets, expo-media-library transitives, etc.) still shipped <uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE" android:maxSdkVersion="32"/> and similar for WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, while another module (or the app) declared the same permission without maxSdkVersion. The ExpoMaxSdkOverride plugin saw two declarations of the same permission with conflicting maxSdkVersion values and printed 'Found 2 permission(s) with conflicting android:maxSdkVersion declarations'. Mitigation applied: add both permissions to expo.android.blockedPermissions in app.json so Expo prebuild emits them with tools:node="remove" — manifest merging then deletes every incoming declaration (both the tagged and untagged copy), leaving the plugin with 0 conflicting declarations to warn about. Verified in /tmp/pb2 manifest. Also, both photo pickers were changed to skip ImagePicker.requestMediaLibraryPermissionsAsync on Android because that call indirectly re-adds a storage permission the system then merges back in — paired change that prevents the warning returning via the pickers. The actual Gradle-time log line can only be confirmed in GitHub Actions.
